Technically every computer breaks dmca because of this thing called ram; the dmca is very poorly written.

Because viewing anything online, copyrighted or otherwise, requires that your computer render a copy of it - this resides in ram. Technically your PC is breaking DMCA by making a copy, even though it's the only way to view the copyrighted material, even legally.
I'm not an expert on American law, but in most countries internal copying within the device is not even considered creating a copy.
It's not here either, the point is that DMCA verbiage is so amateur that the copy residing in ram fits the bill of a prosecuatble offense.
